## Introduction

This blog post explores the beer_markets dataset, which contains information about beer purchases, pricing, packaging, geographic markets, and household demographics.

The analysis focuses on patterns in consumer beer purchasing behavior, including how beer volume, promotions, brands, and household characteristics relate to beer spending and pricing.

```{r}

library(tidyverse)

beer_markets <- read_csv(
  "https://bcdanl.github.io/data/beer_markets_all_cleaned.csv"
)

```

## Descriptive Statistics

```{r}

colnames(beer_markets)

beer_markets %>%
  summarise(
    avg_spending = mean(dollar_spent, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_quantity = mean(quantity, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_price = mean(price_floz, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

## Counting

```{r}

# Popular brand

beer_markets %>%
  count(brand, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(10)

```

## Filtering

```{r}

# Promotional purchases

promo_beers <- beer_markets %>%
  filter(promo == 1)

promo_beers %>%
  summarise(
    avg_spending = mean(dollar_spent, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

## Grouped summaries

```{r}

beer_markets %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_spending = mean(dollar_spent, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_quantity = mean(quantity, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

## Regression models

```{r}

model1 <- lm(
  log(price_floz) ~
    market +
    brand +
    container +
    log(beer_floz),
  data = beer_markets
)

model2 <- lm(
  log(price_floz) ~
    market +
    brand +
    container +
    log(beer_floz) +
    brand:log(beer_floz),
  data = beer_markets
)

library(stargazer)

stargazer(
  model1,
  model2,
  type = "text"
)

library(modelsummary)

modelsummary(
  list(
    "Model 1" = model1,
    "Model 2" = model2
  ),
  statistic = "std.error",
  stars = TRUE,
  output = "markdown"
)


```

## ggplot visualization

```{r}

log(price_floz) ~ log(beer_floz)

beer_markets |>
  filter(
    container %in% c("CAN", "NON_REFILLABLE_BOTTLE"),
    price_floz > 0,
    beer_floz > 0
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = beer_floz, y = price_floz)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Beer Volume and Price per Fluid Ounce",
    subtitle = "Larger beer purchases tend to have lower unit prices",
    x = "Beer Volume (fluid ounces, log scale)",
    y = "Price per Fluid Ounce (log scale)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

The plot shows a negative relationship between beer volume and price per fluid ounce. Larger beer purchases tend to have lower unit prices, suggesting a quantity discount pattern in beer markets.
